per_video_records.brain_regions: Dorsal Striatum (Basal Ganglia) vs Medial Temporal Hippocampus

per_video_records.hook_sentence: In 2023 at Stanford University, a sixty-eight-year-old woman with paralysis named Pat sat unable to speak clearly for eleven years.
per_video_records.protagonist: Participant T12 (Pat Bennett, examined by Willett, Henderson & Shenoy)
per_video_records.brain_regions: Ventral Premotor Speech Cortex (vPMC) vs Corticobulbar Brainstem Tract

per_video_records.title: Two Conscious Minds Inside One Human Skull
per_video_records.hook_sentence: In the 1960s at Caltech, neuroscientist Michael Gazzaniga tested patient WJ after surgeons severed the main cable between his two brain halves.
per_video_records.protagonist: Split-brain patients WJ and PS (examined by Gazzaniga & Sperry)
per_video_records.brain_regions: Corpus Callosum Midline Bridge between Left and Right Cerebral Hemispheres

per_video_records.title: The Iron Rod That Rewired Human Personality
per_video_records.hook_sentence: In 1848 in Cavendish, Vermont, an accidental blast drove a thirteen-pound iron tamping rod straight through railroad foreman Phineas Gage's skull.
per_video_records.protagonist: Phineas Gage (reconstructed by Hanna & Antonio Damasio, 1994)

per_video_records.title: Why Your Brain Rewrites Reality to Protect Your Ego
per_video_records.hook_sentence: In 2009 at Stanford and Caltech, Vincent van Veen placed volunteers inside an fMRI scanner and asked them to call an uncomfortable scanner test enjoyable.
per_video_records.protagonist: fMRI participants in van Veen, Krug, Schooler & Carter (2009)
per_video_records.brain_regions: Dorsal Anterior Cingulate Cortex (dACC), Anterior Insula, and Prefrontal Cortex

per_video_records.title: What One Sleepless Night Does to Your Brain
per_video_records.hook_sentence: In 2013 at the University of Rochester, Maiken Nedergaard's team imaged living brains to solve why every animal dies without sleep.
per_video_records.protagonist: Maiken Nedergaard & Lulu Xie research team
per_video_records.brain_regions: Cortical Perivascular Glymphatic Channels and Interstitial Space

per_video_records.title: The Silicon Chip That Boosted Human Memory 37%
per_video_records.hook_sentence: In 2018 at Wake Forest and USC, neuroscientists tested a silicon memory prosthesis in surgical patients whose temporal lobes were struggling to store new events.
per_video_records.protagonist: Epilepsy surgical patients (examined by Hampson, Song, Deadwyler & Berger)
per_video_records.brain_regions: Hippocampal CA3 Input Layer to CA1 Output Layer in Medial Temporal Lobe

per_video_records.title: When You Believe Your Family Are Imposters
per_video_records.hook_sentence: In the 1990s, a young man named DS survived a car crash and a severe head injury. Then he made a chilling claim about his parents.
per_video_records.brain_regions: Fusiform Face Area (FFA) in ventral temporal cortex to Limbic Amygdala

per_video_records.title: How One Word Rewrites Human Memory
per_video_records.hook_sentence: In 1974 at the University of Washington, Elizabeth Loftus showed witnesses film clips of car crashes and changed one single word in her question.
per_video_records.protagonist: Eyewitness participants in Loftus & Palmer (1974) car-crash study
per_video_records.brain_regions: Medial Temporal Hippocampus and Prefrontal Reconsolidation Network

per_video_records.title: Why Your Brain Deletes Objects Right in Front of You
per_video_records.hook_sentence: In 1999 at Harvard University, Daniel Simons and Christopher Chabris asked volunteers to count basketball passes on a screen while a gorilla walked through.
per_video_records.protagonist: Observers in Simons & Chabris Invisible Gorilla experiment
per_video_records.brain_regions: Dorsal Frontoparietal Attention Network and Thalamic Reticular Nucleus (TRN)
